newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to allow Ireland to delay telecoms opening.
newsitem.headline: EU to allow Ireland to delay telecoms opening.

text.p: The European Commission is expected to grant soon an Irish request to delay the full liberalisation of its telecommunications market until January 1, 2000, two years later than most of its European Union partners.

But the Commission will require Ireland to allow so-called alternative telecoms networks, operated by some utility companies, to carry liberalised services earlier than it wanted, Commission sources said on Friday.

Ireland asked the Commission in June for permission to delay opening that market until July 1, 1999. But the Commission's draft decision gives it until July 1, 1997 only -- one year past the general deadline.

In a decision which could be adopted as early as next week, the Commission will also force Ireland to allow mobile telephone operators to interconnect their networks with other mobile or fixed networks from January 1, 1999, the sources said.
That is one year earlier than requested by Dublin, but almost three years later than required for most of the rest of the EU.

The Commission sources would not explain why Ireland's requests were not fully accepted. The Irish government had argued that state-owned Telecom Eireann needed the extra time to adapt to a fully liberalised market.

But at the end of June, it sold a 20-percent strategic stake in the telecoms monopoly to a consortium formed by Dutch telecoms group KPN and Telia AB of Sweden which was seen as boosting the development of Telecom Eireann.
Under EU rules, the telecoms markets in most countries will be entirely open to competition from January 1, 1998.

Ireland and some other small EU markets -- Portugal, Luxembourg and Greece -- were allowed extra time if justified. The other three countries are waiting for Commission clearance of exemptions to the agreed deadlines.

Spain was also given the possibility to seek more time. But under pressure from the Commission, which deemed it too big to remain closed to competition, it has now agreed to open its market to full and effective competition by November 30, 1998.
